MeasureTheory.QuotientMeasureEqMeasurePreimage and Weil's integration formula for a closed normal subgroup (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Haar/), plus independence of the fundamental domain

AA.2: a_G and H_G with product-formula vanishing, invariant quotient measures via Weil's formula for non-normal closed subgroups, central characters and L^2 spaces, Tamagawa measures from invariant differential forms.

AA.3: all of reduction theory - minimal rational parabolics, relative chambers, Siegel sets and height estimates, finite covering by Siegel sets, finite volume, the anisotropic compactness criterion, finiteness of the class set.
AA.4-AA.5: weak/strong approximation for general groups, neat-level covering maps and Hecke Cartesian diagrams, the idele-class and upper-half-plane identifications.

Imported and also missing: ReductiveGroupsPartII (topologies on rational points of algebraic groups over local fields, Weil restriction and the Deligne torus, integral compact subgroups) and ModularCurvesPartII R12.2 for the GL_2 validation.

judgements.reason: Both are essentially finished in the baseline, but Multiquadratic has no residue at all (sqrtTower, the splitting law, the ambiguous class number formula, isGenusField_candidateGenusField and narrowTwoRank_eq_ncard_ramifiedPrimes_sub_one are all proved sorry-free), whereas Exchangeability still owes the jointly exchangeable Aldous-Hoover representation: only separatelyExchangeable_iff_exists_coding exists, and for jointly exchangeable arrays just jointlyExchangeable_iff and the dissociated/ergodic direction.

RootSystems' only real gap is packaging Tits' presentation - weylCoxeterHom is already proved surjective and the exchange/subword combinatorics (strongExchange, exists_sublist_wordProd_eq_and_length_eq_ncard_inversions) that gives injectivity is built - plus the Matsumoto lift form, while Exchangeability still needs a genuinely new theorem, the coding representation for jointly exchangeable arrays.

Coding theory has five whole layers unbuilt - dual codes and minimum distance, weight enumerators and MacWilliams, Type II theory, the tetracode/hexacode/Golay constructions, Construction A and the discriminant-module bridge - while RootSystems is missing only the injectivity half of Tits' theorem, length = #inversions and the Matsumoto lift, on top of an already-proved classification and simply connected root data.

AdelicAlgebraicGroups must first obtain topologies on rational points of reductive groups and Weil restriction from ReductiveGroupsPartII, then build G(A) as a topological group, Haar and Tamagawa measures on restricted products, a_G and H_G, and the whole of reduction theory (Siegel sets, finite volume, anisotropic compactness, finiteness of the class set); the coding roadmap needs only elementary finite algebra - duality, MacWilliams, four explicit codes, Construction A - over Mathlib's Hamming API and TauCeti's already-built integral-lattice discriminant theory.

GN.3 already needs the reduction domains, arithmetic quotients and Haar normalisations that are AdelicAlgebraicGroups' whole content, and then adds Hasse-Minkowski with Witt/Hilbert/Clifford invariants, genera and spinor genera, mass formulas and theta series, unipotent-flow and nondivergence dynamics for GN.4, LLL certificates, and hermitian K-theory built on GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.4/K.6; GN also starts from more - Mathlib already has GN.0 and Minkowski's convex-body theorem.

Geometric topology has nine of its eleven layers untouched and its spine is absent - no boundary-as-manifold, collars in general, gluing along a face, handle attachment, tubular neighbourhoods or connected sum - so surgery, concordance, Riemannian volume and curvature, the eight geometries with JSJ, Heegaard genus and foliation Euler classes all sit on nothing; geometry of numbers starts from Mathlib's ZLattice.covolume and Minkowski's convex-body theorem and TauCeti's Witt theory, though it still owes Hasse-Minkowski, genera and mass formulas, homogeneous dynamics and hermitian K-theory.

Locally symmetric spaces need every stage of AdelicAlgebraicGroups up to reduction theory before ALS.0 can even define X_K, then Cartan involutions and symmetric spaces, the Borel-Serre manifold-with-corners compactification, Hecke correspondences lifted to the derived category and Verdier duality - and the cochain-level cup products and Poincare-Lefschetz duality it consumes are absent from the baseline too (zero hits for cupProduct or poincareDuality); geometric topology is broader but self-contained, and TauCeti already has combinatorial spheres/balls and collapse for its Layer 11 and IsLocallyFlat and PLGroupoid for Layers 1-2.

Even leaving aside its nonabelian-Chabauty top stage, EffectiveDiophantineMethods pulls in 87 upstream stages across 32 roadmaps: certified algebraic numbers, LLL via GeometryOfNumbers GN.5, explicit Baker-Matveev constants via DT.3, the height machine and weak Mordell-Weil, Coleman integration with Frobenius continuation and scheme/stack foundations; ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces is a single deep tower of 49 upstream stages over AdelicAlgebraicGroups and real-group theory.

EffectiveDiophantineMethods needs much of the Euler-system roadmap's own base - ArithmeticGaloisDuality, SelmerIwasawaCohomology and PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras all appear in its closure for the descent and saturation stage - and then adds LLL and geometry of numbers, explicit linear forms in logarithms, Coleman integration over rigid cohomology, Chabauty and the Mordell-Weil sieve; Euler systems stay inside Galois cohomology and Iwasawa algebra, deep but narrower, with Chebotarev and class field theory already partly in TauCeti.

Arakelov theory cannot state the Faltings height until abelian schemes, Neron models and semistable reduction, PEL moduli and Shimura compactifications all exist - none of them does, and 'Arakelov', 'Faltings' and 'arithmeticDegree' have zero occurrences in the baseline - which is 91 upstream stages over 26 roadmaps; Euler systems need Poitou-Tate duality, Iwasawa algebras and Selmer complexes, 46 upstream stages over 15 roadmaps, on a base where Chebotarev and class field theory formation are already built.

Their upstreams overlap in 23 roadmaps, but AutomorphicBundles needs strictly more of the Shimura tower (10 ShimuraVarieties stages including the general-data canonical models against Arakelov's 8, and 9 ShimuraCompactifications stages against 6, plus HilbertModularVarieties) and then owns Milne's canonical principal bundle, a new theorem beyond canonical models, together with canonical and subcanonical extensions; Arakelov's extra requirement is only Neron models and semistable reduction on top of a shared base.

Igusa varieties consume AutomorphicBundles' output and then require perfectoid Shimura varieties, diamonds with their six operations and etale cohomology, perverse sheaves and nearby cycles, PEL integral models with Newton strata and central leaves, and the endoscopic unitary trace comparison - none of which AutomorphicBundles needs, and none of which exists in the baseline.
